name: Pluto
tagline: The beloved dwarf — king of the Kuiper Belt and a world of nitrogen glaciers.
history: Clyde Tombaugh found Pluto in 1930 after a systematic search for 'Planet X', and for 76 years it counted as the ninth planet. The IAU's 2006 definition reclassified it as a dwarf planet — the first recognized member of the Kuiper Belt, the ring of icy bodies beyond Neptune. NASA's New Horizons spacecraft flew within 12,500 km in July 2015 and revealed a surprisingly active world: a heart-shaped nitrogen-ice plain (Sputnik Planitia) that convects like a lava lamp, water-ice mountains up to 3.5 km high, and a thin blue haze atmosphere. Its largest moon Charon is half Pluto's size — a true double system.
source: NASA/JPL Solar System Exploration; Johns Hopkins APL
